cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: Rich Romans lived in domus (single-family houses) with atrium, peristyle gardens and private baths

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: Most Romans lived in insulae (multi-storey apartment blocks) — cramped, fire-prone and overcrowded

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: The typical Roman day began at dawn, with business conducted in the morning and leisure in the afternoon

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: Roman meals: ientaculum (breakfast), prandium (light lunch), cena (main evening meal)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: The cena for wealthy Romans could be an elaborate multi-course banquet with exotic foods

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: Roman baths (thermae) were social centres for exercise, bathing, business and relaxation

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: Men wore the toga (citizens) or tunic; women wore the stola (married women) or palla

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: Roman children were educated at home or in schools — boys could pursue higher education, girls rarely did

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: Marriage was a social and economic arrangement — the paterfamilias arranged matches for his children

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: Slaves performed domestic work, skilled crafts and agricultural labour — their treatment varied enormously

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: Public latrines, aqueducts and sewers (Cloaca Maxima) made Rome relatively hygienic for an ancient city

cards.front: Recall a key point about Daily Life in Rome
cards.back: The forum was the centre of public life — markets, law courts, temples and political speeches
